title: add-per-feature-stability-benchmark-and-rolling-sanity-ci-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: teams have asked for finer-grained regression signals beyond aggregate metrics. This PR introduces a per-feature stability benchmarking module plus a rolling 'sanity' CI adapter that monitors short-term drift and flags PRs likely to cause regressions in specific feature slices (e.g., intent categories, length-buckets, and language tags). The goal is to provide earlier, actionable feedback in the PR cycle without blocking merges for small, explainable variance. What this change implements: 1) a lightweight per-feature stability scorer that computes delta distributions over a sliding window and exposes a compact JSON report; 2) a simulation harness that runs perturbation scenarios (paraphrase/noise/tokenization edgecases) against the candidate patch to surface brittle prompt-sets; 3) a rolling-sanity CI adapter which (a) runs daily on the main branch to compute baseline stability snapshots, (b) runs on PRs to compare candidate deltas against the baseline and historical variance, and (c) sets a GitHub Check with results and an annotated comment suggesting follow-ups (soft-fail thresholds, recommended prompt subsets to re-eval, and suggested rollback ranges). The adapter is tuned to be conservative by default (soft-fail/report-only) with a configurable mode for stricter teams. Backwards compatibility: existing eval pipelines continue to work; new module plugs into the eval-harness plugin registry and exposes a simple CLI and pytest fixtures. Related: touches eval-harness integration with the CI checks orchestrator and the prompt metadata schema so teams must tag prompts with feature keys to get per-feature signals.

ff9a1b4: add ci/adapters/rolling_sanity_adapter.py and GH checks integration, include soft-fail policy
d7e6a2c: tests + docs: stable examples, usage guide, and migration notes for prompt metadata

release_notes: Adds per-feature stability scoring and a rolling sanity CI adapter. New tooling surfaces slice-level regressions and provides recommendation comments on PRs. Default behavior is report-only; teams can opt-in to stricter enforcement. Includes docs and example prompt metadata for per-feature tagging.
qa_summary: Unit and integration tests added; local smoke runs show a median runtime of ~22s for the per-feature scorer on a 2k prompt set. Staging daily job ran for 2025-11-17 and produced baseline snapshot; no blocking alerts triggered. One flaky test was fixed by seeding randomness in perturbation harness.
notes_for_ops: Adapter stores baseline snapshots in /data/eval-baselines/{branch}/per-feature.json and expects 30-day retention. Ops should ensure the CI runner has 2GB free disk for snapshot caches. Default window=7 days; adjustable via EVAL_SANITY_WINDOW env var.
rationale: We observed regressions that only affected narrow slices and were hidden by aggregate pass/fail rules. This PR provides higher signal-to-noise actionable telemetry and reduces time-to-detect for slice-specific regressions without increasing merge friction by default.
